subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should WebChat `chat.send` ACK only after the user turn is durably recorded or otherwise guaranteed to progress, or should OpenClaw keep the current fast ACK and rely on later runtime/fallback persistence plus UI preservation?
rationale: Both choices affect latency, transcript ownership, duplicate suppression, and recovery semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent contract while the open gateway PR is unresolved.

options.title: Require Durable/Progress ACK
options.body: Make `chat.send` ACK contingent on a durable user-turn record or an explicit progress guarantee, then port the candidate fix through the shared recorder boundary.

options.title: Keep Fast ACK With Visible Failure
options.body: Preserve fast ACK but add explicit user-visible failure/audit behavior for any post-ACK path that cannot durably record or dispatch the turn.

options.title: Close Candidate Direction
options.body: Reject eager durability for now and keep this issue open only if a narrower live repro shows current UI and fallback behavior still loses messages.

recommendation.title: Require Durable/Progress ACK
recommendation.body: Make `chat.send` ACK contingent on a durable user-turn record or an explicit progress guarantee, then port the candidate fix through the shared recorder boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is centered on the shared user-turn recorder and transcript persistence boundary they recently authored.
